issues.body: The module promises that an unusable API payload exits 2 and that there is no exit 1, but collect_fixture does not validate each runs entry or that runs/jobs are lists, and decompose_run calls job.get before decompose_job can validate the item. For example, a fixture with runs containing null raises AttributeError at run.get, while jobs containing null raises at job.get; main catches only InventoryError, so both leak a traceback and exit 1. Equivalent malformed list shapes from the API have the same problem. This directly contradicts the documented fail-loud behavior for unusable payloads.
issues.fix_hint: Validate that runs and jobs are lists and that every run/job is an object before accessing .get, raising InventoryError with context on failure. Add CLI-level tests for malformed run and job entries asserting exit 2, empty stdout, and a concise stderr diagnostic. Also validate the workflow_runs and jobs collections returned by _gh before slicing or iterating.
issues.title: Malformed payload shapes violate the no-exit-1 contract

verdict.summary: The accounting and classification paths are well covered and the 56-test hermetic suite passes, but the advertised fail-loud exit contract is incomplete: malformed fixture/API container shapes escape as ordinary Python exceptions and produce exit 1 with a traceback instead of the promised diagnostic exit 2. Because handling unusable payloads is a stated load-bearing contract of this measurement tool, this needs correction before approval.
